classification.difficultyReason: Link same-chord angles across two circles through a vertically opposite pair.

content.prompt: Two circles intersect at $T$ and $V$. The intervals $PTQ$ and $RTS$ are drawn as shown. Prove that $\angle PVR=\angle QVS$.

spec.description: Two intersecting circles with straight PTQ and RTS, and four chords from V.
spec.mathematics: T,V are exact circle intersections; other points are second secant intersections with their respective circles.
spec.answerVisibility: Original givens and necessary labels only; no calculated answers.

sizing.exceptionReason: Proof construction, source relationships and full10pt labels determine size; final width and height require source-side rendered review.

answer.worked:
Let $\angle PVR=\alpha$. In the left circle, $\angle PTR=\alpha$ (angles subtended by chord $PR$).

Since $PTQ$ and $RTS$ are straight, $\angle QTS=\angle PTR=\alpha$ (vertically opposite angles).

In the right circle, $\angle QVS=\angle QTS$ (angles subtended by chord $QS$). Therefore $\angle QVS=\angle PVR$.
